key_insight: Tokeniser construction can be cast as a convex (linear) optimisation problem instead of greedy local heuristics; solving this relaxation (ConvexTok) yields vocabularies that improve intrinsic tokenisation metrics and reduce bits‑per‑byte (BpB).
problem_solved: Greedy tokenisation algorithms (e.g., BPE, Unigram) make locally optimal splits and merges without a global view, producing suboptimal vocabularies that hurt compression and token efficiency.
method: Formulate vocabulary selection and token assignments as a linear program that captures global tradeoffs across the corpus.
Relax the discrete selection constraints to a convex problem and solve with standard convex optimisation tools to obtain a continuous solution (ConvexTok).
Post-process the relaxed solution (rounding/pruning) to produce a discrete tokeniser and evaluate using intrinsic metrics and bits‑per‑byte (BpB).
impact: ConvexTok provides a principled, globally aware way to build tokenisers that lower BpB and improve tokenisation quality—helpful for model size, training efficiency, multilingual and low‑resource settings.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side diagram: greedy tokeniser (local decisions) vs ConvexTok (global optimisation) showing different vocab outcomes
Pipeline flowchart: corpus → LP formulation → convex solver → rounding → tokeniser
Bar chart or line plot: BpB and intrinsic metric comparisons (ConvexTok vs BPE/Unigram) across datasets
Heatmap or matrix: soft token assignment weights from the convex relaxation to illustrate global allocation
paper_authors: Jan Tempus, Philip Whittington, Craig W. Schmidt, Dennis Komm, Tiago Pimentel
